rule: Lighting a lantern produces mist-light
texts: When a lantern burns mire-essence, the lantern produces mist-light.
If a lantern burns mire-essence, the lantern gives mist-light.
Mist-light is a pale silver flame.
Ordinary oil does not produce mist-light.

rule: Mist-light attracts nightmoths
texts: When a lantern shows mist-light at night, the mist-light attracts nightmoths.
If a lantern shows mist-light at night, the mist-light draws nightmoths.
Nightmoths do not see ordinary firelight.
Nightmoths rarely fly on cold nights.

rule: Nightmoths landing on lanterns leave silken threads
texts: When a nightmoth lands on a lantern, the nightmoth leaves silken threads on the lantern.
If a nightmoth rests on a lantern, the nightmoth sheds silken threads onto the lantern.
Silken threads come from the undersides of nightmoths.

rule: Silken threads boiled in sea-water yield mire-essence
texts: When the Keepers boil silken threads in sea-water, mire-essence forms in the cauldron.
If the Keepers boil silken threads in sea-water, the cauldron yields mire-essence.
The Keepers take the sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Fresh water does not yield mire-essence.

rule: Stored mire-essence feeds future lighting
texts: When mire-essence forms in the cauldron, the Keepers store the mire-essence in clay vessels.
If mire-essence forms in the cauldron, the Keepers keep the mire-essence in clay vessels.
The Keepers draw stored mire-essence when they tend lanterns.
Stored mire-essence feeds future lantern lighting.

rule: A crowd of nightmoths brings sky-cats down
texts: When many nightmoths gather at a lantern-row, sky-cats descend from the cliff-spires.
If many nightmoths crowd a lantern-row, sky-cats descend from the cliff-spires.
When few nightmoths gather at a lantern-row, sky-cats stay on the cliff-spires.

rule: Sky-cats hunting reduces nightmoth populations
texts: When sky-cats descend, the sky-cats hunt nightmoths.
When sky-cats hunt nightmoths, the nightmoth crowd at that lantern-row shrinks.
If sky-cats hunt nightmoths, the nightmoth crowd at that lantern-row thins.
After a sky-cat hunt, the thread harvest at that lantern-row falls.

rule: Hunted nightmoths flee to dimmer lights
texts: When sky-cats hunt at a lantern-row, the surviving nightmoths flee toward dimmer lanterns.
If sky-cats hunt at a lantern-row, the surviving nightmoths move to the Hollows.
When fleeing nightmoths reach the Hollows, the Hollows lanterns gain extra silken threads.

rule: Sky-cats roost on the cliff-spires by day
texts: Sky-cats roost on the cliff-spires during the day.
Sky-cats do not enter the village.
The Keepers tolerate sky-cats.

rule: Sky-cats molt feathers to the cliff base
texts: When sky-cats molt, feathers fall to the cliff base.
If sky-cats molt, the sky-cats shed feathers onto the cliff base.
Apprentices collect the fallen feathers in the morning.
The Keepers store the collected feathers in a bin at the Watch.

rule: Untended lanterns die before dawn
texts: When a Keeper leaves a lantern untended overnight, the lantern dies before dawn.
If a lantern stays untended through the night, the lantern goes out before dawn.
A Keeper refreshes the mire-essence and trims the wick during the night.

rule: Dead lanterns at the Sunken Cove raise wraiths
texts: When a lantern at the Sunken Cove dies before dawn, a wraith emerges from the cove water.
If a lantern at the Sunken Cove goes out at night, a wraith rises from the cove water.
Lanterns elsewhere do not raise wraiths when they die.
The Sunken Cove is the village's drowned graveyard.

rule: Wraiths drain mire-essence from lit lanterns
texts: When a wraith approaches a lit lantern, the wraith drains mire-essence from the lantern.
If a wraith nears a lit lantern, the wraith pulls mire-essence from the lantern.
A drained lantern burns dimly.

rule: Drained lanterns give weak mist-light
texts: When a wraith drains a lantern, the lantern gives weak mist-light.
If a wraith drains a lantern, the lantern shows dim mist-light.
Weak mist-light rarely attracts nightmoths.
When lanterns attract few nightmoths, the thread harvest falls.

rule: Ground feathers ward lanterns from wraiths
texts: When the Keepers scatter ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers ward the lantern from wraiths.
If the Keepers spread ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers shield the lantern from wraiths.
Wraiths do not approach a warded lantern.
Fresh ground feathers ward a lantern.
Stale ground feathers do not ward a lantern.

rule: Cold winds extinguish unprepared lanterns
texts: When cold wind blows off the sea at night, the cold wind extinguishes unprepared lanterns.
If cold wind strikes the Cliff Path at night, unprepared lanterns go out.
Lanterns in shielded coves stay safe from cold winds.

rule: Salt-bloom in winter slows the burn
texts: When the Keepers add salt-bloom to mire-essence in winter, the mire-essence burns slowly.
If the Keepers mix salt-bloom into mire-essence in winter, the mire-essence burns slowly.
A salt-bloomed lantern resists cold wind.

rule: Salt-bloom is harvested at new moon
texts: When the Keepers harvest salt-bloom at the new moon, the salt-bloom keeps its potency.
If the Keepers gather salt-bloom at the new moon, the salt-bloom stays potent.
When the Keepers gather salt-bloom at other moon phases, the salt-bloom turns to chalky residue.

rule: Spring tides bloom salt-bloom in the tide-pools
texts: When a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom blooms in the tide-pools.
If a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom grows in the tide-pools.
Salt-bloom is a pale crystalline crust.
The bloom soon dissolves into the seawater.

rule: Spring tides occur near new moon and full moon
texts: Spring tides occur near the new moon.
Spring tides occur near the full moon.
The Keepers time the salt-bloom harvest to the new-moon spring tide.

rule: Wintergloss repels nightmoths
texts: When wintergloss burns in a lantern, the wintergloss repels nightmoths from that lantern.
If wintergloss burns alongside mire-essence, nightmoths avoid that lantern.
The Keepers rarely burn wintergloss.
The Keepers sometimes burn wintergloss at the Stilllight Lantern.

rule: Cliff-spires shield the Northcove
texts: When cliff-spires shield a cove from north winds, lanterns in that cove burn stably through winter.
If cliff-spires block the north wind from a cove, lanterns in that cove stay lit through winter.
The Northcove is the shielded cove of Aelmere.
Northcove lanterns never go out in cold winds.

rule: Keepers inherit lantern-stations
texts: When a senior Keeper retires, an heir inherits the lantern-station.
If a senior Keeper dies, an heir inherits the lantern-station.
An inherited station stays in the family.
The Council must approve any station transfer.

rule: Newcomers apprentice under a senior Keeper
texts: A newcomer must apprentice under a senior Keeper.
A new apprentice does not tend a lantern alone.
The Council permits an apprentice to begin solo tending.

rule: Sustained solo tending completes apprenticeship
texts: When an apprentice completes many solo nights of tending, the Council invests the apprentice as a Keeper.
If the apprentice's lantern fails, the solo count resets.
If the apprentice's lantern dims, the solo count resets.

rule: The Council convenes at full moon
texts: When the moon is full, the Council convenes at the Watch.
If the moon is full, the Council meets at the Watch.
The Council rarely meets at other times.

rule: The Council redistributes mire-essence
texts: When the Council convenes, the Council redistributes mire-essence across the lantern-stations.
If the Council meets, the Council reallocates mire-essence among the lantern-stations.
Productive stations contribute mire-essence to a central pool.
Burdened stations draw mire-essence from the central pool.
The Keepers record the redistribution in the Watch ledgers.

rule: Summer hunting yields the autumn feather store
texts: When sky-cats hunt often through summer, many feathers accumulate at the cliff base by autumn.
If sky-cats hunt often in summer, the autumn feather store grows.
Frequent hunting causes frequent molting.

rule: Large feather stores enable safe Sunken-Cove tending
texts: When the feather store at the Watch is large, the Keepers tend the Sunken Cove lanterns safely in winter.
If the Watch holds a large feather store, winter tending at the Sunken Cove stays safe.
The Council issues feather rations to the Sunken-Cove station in winter.
When the feather store is small, wraith risk grows.

rule: Wraith activity prompts feather-ration requests
texts: When wraith activity at the Sunken Cove increases, the neighboring stations request feather rations from the Council.
If wraith sightings at the Sunken Cove rise, the stations ask the Council for feather rations.
The Council weighs the requests against the central feather store.
The Council prioritizes stations with drained lanterns.
